title: Global minimum cut

problem.name: Global minimum cut
problem.statement_latex:
In a weighted undirected graph, output a nonempty proper subset $S\subset V$ minimizing $w(\delta(S))=\sum_{u\in S,v\notin S}w_{uv}$. This identifies the cheapest edge failure that disconnects a network.
The quantum comparison counts weighted adjacency queries and running time; classical bounds refer to explicit weighted graphs.
problem.statement_text: In a weighted undirected graph, output a nonempty proper subset $S\subset V$ minimizing $w(\delta(S))=\sum_{u\in S,v\notin S}w_{uv}$. This identifies the cheapest edge failure that disconnects a network. The quantum comparison counts weighted adjacency queries and running time; classical bounds refer to explicit weighted graphs.

quantum.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(n^{3/2}\sqrt\tau)$ matrix time and queries, quantum minimum cut.
quantum.details_latex: Here $\tau$ is the ratio of the largest to smallest positive weight; reading the matrix caps the bound at $O(n^2)$. In the adjacency-array model, the query bound is $\widetilde O(\sqrt{mn\tau})$ and the time bound is $\widetilde O(\sqrt{mn\tau}+n^{3/2})$. The algorithm returns the minimum-cut weight and shores. Approximate cuts can instead use quantum cut sparsification.

classical.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(m)$ expected time, randomized classical minimum cut; $\Theta(n^2)$ matrix queries.
classical.details_latex: The explicit-input comparison includes randomized contraction and near-linear cut algorithms. The matrix quantum lower bound is $\Omega(n^{3/2}\sqrt\tau)$ in the nontrivial range $1\le\tau\le n$, up to the precision and logarithmic conventions of the theorem.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial oracle improvement; for bounded weight ratio and dense graphs it is $n^2\to\widetilde O(n^{3/2})$.

hardware.description_latex: Fault-tolerant search and sparsification require logarithmic vertex registers, weight registers and coherent graph-access workspace. A classical sparse graph and contracted partitions are stored during the computation.
